summary.name: Marp
summary.one_liner: Marp (Markdown Presentation Ecosystem) is a toolset that turns Markdown documents into slide decks that can be exported to HTML, PDF, and PowerPoint.
use_cases: Writing slide decks as plain Markdown text
Exporting presentations to HTML, PDF, or PowerPoint
Previewing slides while editing in VS Code
Converting Markdown slides from the command line or in batch
Customizing slide design with CSS themes
summary.what_it_does: Marp uses CommonMark-based Markdown, where a horizontal rule (---) separates slides. It supports directives and extended syntax such as image syntax, math typesetting, and auto-scaling. It ships three built-in themes (default, gaia, uncover) and allows styling changes via Markdown or custom themes written in plain CSS. Marp converts decks to HTML, PDF, and PowerPoint, using Google Chrome or Chromium for the conversion. The ecosystem includes Marp for VS Code, Marp CLI, and Marp Core, all built on the Marpit framework, which has a pluggable architecture.
notable: Slides are written as Markdown, with --- splitting pages
Built on the Marpit framework with a pluggable plugin architecture
All official tools and libraries are MIT-licensed
Built-in themes default, gaia, and uncover, plus custom CSS themes
caveats: PDF and PowerPoint export relies on Google Chrome or Chromium being available
